rules.title: How we count
items: With/without spaces: counts visible characters (Unicode graphemes). Family emoji, flags and combining marks count as one.
Bytes (Korean = 2): same as the JobKorea/Saramin counters. Non-ASCII characters are 2 bytes; letters, digits, keyboard symbols (. , ! ? etc.), spaces and line breaks are 1 byte; emoji are 4 bytes.
UTF-8 bytes: Korean 3 bytes, ASCII 1 byte, emoji 4 bytes. Useful for server/database storage limits.
Sentences split after . ! ? … followed by a space or a line break (numbers like 3.14 are not split). Paragraphs are separated by blank lines.

Manuscript: simplified 200-cell Korean manuscript paper (20 × 10). Each line break starts a paragraph with one indent cell; two lowercase letters or digits share a cell. Fine rules such as end-of-line punctuation are skipped, so results may be off by a few cells.
Reading/speaking time: estimated at 500 / 250 Korean characters per minute and 238 / 150 English words per minute.
X weighted length: follows X's official twitter-text (v3) rules — Latin letters and digits 1, Korean/CJK and emoji 2, links starting with http 23. The limit is 280.

whatIs.title: What is the Character Counter?
whatIs.description: View character counts with or without whitespace, bytes, words, sentences, paragraphs, lines and reading time. Manage titles, text, counting bases and goals across 5 questions, preserving fields edited while drafts load. Cleanup, version restores and copy requests are separated from later edits.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Choose question 1–5, optionally add a title, and type or paste text to update the statistics.
Set the counting basis and goal, then compare them with the actual requirements of your destination.
Undo the valid latest cleanup or version restore in its original question. A new edit to that question invalidates the old undo.
If copying fails, select the full text captured by the click or retry. Text is not automatically sent to an external spelling checker.
Storage can fail and saving just before closing is not guaranteed. Keep important work in a version JSON backup or a separate file. Resetting all drafts removes only the automatic draft.

tips.title: Tips
items: Companies differ on with/without spaces or bytes. Match the target to the wording on the application form.
Byte limits usually count Korean as 2 bytes, so 1,000 bytes is about 500 Korean characters. ASCII letters, digits and spaces are 1 byte.
If lines broke when copying from a PDF or HWP file, use 'Join broken lines' to restore paragraphs.
A word used more than three times feels repetitive. Click it in the repeated-words list to see where it appears.

items.a: This tool counts each emoji as one visible character (including family and flag emoji). JobKorea/Saramin count an emoji as 2 characters and 4 bytes and X counts it as 2, so when emoji are present we also show the site-style count.

items.q: Why do byte counts differ between sites?
items.a: Some count a Korean character as 2 bytes (JobKorea, Saramin, SMS) while UTF-8 uses 3 bytes. We show both so you can use whichever your destination requires.

items.q: Is my text saved or uploaded?
items.a: The tool attempts to save valid drafts in this browser without automatically sending them to a server. Storage access or writes can fail, so keep a separate copy of important text. Resetting all drafts only removes the automatic draft; saved versions and backups are separate.

items.q: What happens if copying fails or I switch questions?
items.a: If copying is not confirmed, select the full text captured by the click or retry explicitly. Switching questions, editing or changing language invalidates feedback and fallback from older requests. A clipboard write already submitted to the operating system cannot be recalled.

items.q: Can I undo cleanup or restoring a saved version?
items.a: Undo applies only to the valid latest operation in its original question. A new edit to that question invalidates it, and it cannot apply to a different question. Undoing a version restore also restores the earlier title, text, counting basis and goal.

items.q: Does the spelling-check button send my text to the external site?
items.a: It opens the external checker and attempts to copy the current text, without automatically sending it in a URL or form. Check opening or copy failure messages and paste only the text you intend to share.

items.q: How do counts with and without spaces differ?
items.a: The inclusive count includes spaces and line breaks. The exclusive count removes whitespace, tabs and line breaks. Select the basis and goal for each question to match the destination requirements.

items.q: Can I compare a saved version with the current text?
items.a: The Compare button on a saved version sends the exact saved and current-question text captured by the click to a new comparison tab. Each document allows up to 50,000 UTF-16 units and expires after 10 minutes. Text is not put in the URL. Review it and explicitly run Compare; existing drafts and saved versions stay unchanged.

items.q: How does the X counting basis work?
items.a: This tool uses a 280-unit limit with weights of 1 for Latin letters and digits, 2 for Korean, Chinese, Japanese and emoji, and 23 for links. This differs from displayed-character counts and UTF-8 bytes.
